title: Space Slugs: Week 2
author: The_Pumpkin_Lady
selftext:
Hi Friends!

Week 2 has ended and she's taken a starting shape! There's still much testing, tuning, and cleanup required, but I'm pretty excited at the rate of progress so far.

The goal of this series is not a flex, or a brag - but to mostly to help keep myself accountable and to document the journey for anybody interested. I'm also very open to design feedback, workflow criticism, and gameplay ideas.

I've outlined my workflows and tools in the [Week 1](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1xn3y8r/space_slugs_week_1/) post.

**Wins**

* Early marketing assets created and a Steam page has been formally submitted for review. I think Opus did a decent job at constructing a trailer based on the gameplay so far.
* I'm pretty happy with the ledger system that Fable created. It helps me structure and sequence the work so that asset generation happens overnight while code and design iteration happen during my active working hours. 
* I've created an asset-pipeline skill that generates a 2D concept card > me for approval > generate model with ComfyUI > import to Unreal & setup mesh. With TRELLIS.2 generation it's about 4 minutes per mesh on a 4090 and about 11 minutes on my old 1080TI. AI has done a great job at enforcing style consistency throughout assets.
* Unreal's Nanite is holding strong; the game is rendering tens of millions of triangles without noticeable frame drop. Performance is steady across high, mid, and low tiers of hardware.

**Observations & Learnings**

* Bipedal locomotion is still horrible and I don't have a good solution. I saw a post earlier and I have experimented with [UniMate](https://github.com/Friedrich-M/UniMate), but Opus + Blender produced better quality. Regardless, everything I've tried results in a pawn that walks like they've shit themselves.
* I think the non-human characters and space theme helps to mask some of the "AI feel"; but maybe it's there and I am just blind to it.
* Week 1 Reddit post engagement was poor. I suspect because I used a static image rather than a video. I feel like our monkey brains like flashing lights and sounds, so I am posting a video this week as a marketing experiment.

Anyway, that's week 2. Bless ♥️

comments.author: Benjamin_Martin41
comments.body: the asset pipeline sounds pretty efficient esp. getting consistent results across different models i'm curious how much manual clean up u usually need after importing them into unreal

replies.author: The_Pumpkin_Lady
replies.body:
At this stage there is 0 manual cleanup, but the tris are around 400k per mesh and I can only get away with this because of nanite.

Tripo and Meshy produce game ready meshes and you can hook the APIs into Claude to automate the pipeline, but I couldn't justify the cost considering the volume of meshes that I want.

replies.author: Benjamin_Martin41
replies.body: zero clean up or pretty impressive are u noticing any tradeoffs in mesh quality compared to Tripo or Meshy?

comments.author: kevin_whitley
comments.body: Nanite is such a sick concept in general.  I'm (obviously using an agent) rolling my own engine, and just last night added in my own flavor of Nanite to allow more complex geometry as you get closer to things.  Mind blowing to watch texture geometry morph in realtime as you drag a slider in-engine!
